title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: customer-managed keys for direct export (Worldwide)
summary: The support-request enablement, encryption prerequisites, licensing and rollout windows are supported by Microsoft's documentation and notice. One descriptive assurance about agents and automated actions is unsubstantiated, and the blanket statement about Exchange Online PowerShell needs narrowing; neither prevents publication.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans customer-managed key protection for eDiscovery direct export.
claims.quote: implementation of customer-managed key (CMK) options, allowing users to manage their own encryption keys for the data included in the direct export workflow in eDiscovery

claims.claim: The roadmap describes CMK as adding to existing Microsoft-managed encryption.
claims.quote: adding to the Microsoft-managed encryption already in place.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enablement is admin-opt-in through a tenant request to Microsoft Support.
claims.quote: Only enabled for specific tenants by request to Microsoft Support

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Enabled direct export packages are encrypted at rest using tenant-specific encryption scopes backed by customer-managed keys.
claims.quote: When enabled, exported investigation data is encrypted at rest using tenant-specific encryption scopes backed by customer-managed keys.

claims.claim: CMK direct export applies to organisations configured for Customer Key through MDEP.
claims.quote: Organizations that configure Customer Key through the Microsoft 365 Data-at-Rest Encryption Platform (MDEP) with a Data Encryption Policy (DEP) in policy assigned status can extend CMK protections to eDiscovery direct export packages.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A DEP must be in PolicyAssigned state via the MDEP onboarding cmdlets.
claims.quote: A Data Encryption Policy (DEP) is in PolicyAssigned state via the Microsoft 365 Data-at-Rest Encryption Platform (MDEP) onboarding cmdlets.

claims.quote: CMK configuration is dynamically validated through MDEP at export time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Direct export proceeds without CMK encryption if CMK is not properly configured through MDEP at export time.
claims.quote: If your tenant does not have CMK properly configured through MDEP at export time, direct export jobs will proceed without CMK encryption.

claims.claim: The Learn page marks CMK direct export as preview.

claims.quote: This encryption applies to direct exports only. Data at rest in an eDiscovery review set isn't included at this time.

claims.claim: The protected export packages are service-held data in eDiscovery storage accounts.
claims.quote: Exported investigation data is stored in eDiscovery storage accounts encrypted with customer-managed keys rather than Microsoft-managed keys.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: The prerequisites include Azure Key Vault configured through the standard Customer Key setup process.
claims.quote: Your organization configured Azure Key Vault following the standard Customer Key setup process.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Customer Key requires two paid Azure subscriptions.
claims.quote: Azure subscriptions: Two paid Azure subscriptions (Free, Trial, Sponsorship, MSDN, or Legacy Support aren't eligible)

claims.claim: Customer Key key custody depends on the administrators managing the keys in the two subscriptions.
claims.quote: As a best practice, have different members of your organization manage one key in each subscription. These subscriptions should be used only to administer encryption keys for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: CMK does not change the 14-day exported-data retention.
claims.quote: Exported data retention remains 14 days, unchanged by CMK.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Search export packages expire 14 days after creation.
claims.quote: Search export packages expire 14 days after you create the export.

claims.claim: Expired search exports and their packaged data are deleted automatically and cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: After 14 days, the export and all data contained in the export package are automatically deleted and can't be recovered.

claims.claim: The feature adds no agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery CMK agent automatic actions'; opened edisc-search-export and read MC1289726. These describe automatic export encryption but give no blanket assurance about agents or autonomous actions.
claims.fix: Remove 'No change: the feature adds no agent or automated action.' Retain 'Encryption is applied by the service during the export.'

claims.claim: The service automatically manages encryption scopes, storage accounts and containers without additional storage configuration.
claims.quote: Encryption scopes, storage accounts, and containers are managed automatically by the service; no additional storage configuration is needed.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate charge specific to CMK on direct export in the pages consulted.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery CMK export pricing license charge'; read edisc-search-export, customer-key-set-up, Customer Key service-description licensing and edisc-billing search excerpts. Found prerequisite and export costs, not a separate CMK-direct-export charge.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft's export prerequisites name no licence or SKU specific to CMK direct export.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery CMK export pricing license charge'; opened edisc-search-export and the Purview service description; read MC1289726. The CMK export prerequisites name enablement, Key Vault and DEP, not a separate SKU.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included through the required Customer Key entitlement.
claims.quote: | Customer Key | Included | Included |

claims.claim: Each user benefiting from Customer Key requires a licence.
claims.quote: Each user who benefits from Customer Key requires a license. Requirements vary by workload.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Customer Key is included in the Microsoft 365, Purview Suite, Information Protection and Governance, and Office 365 plans listed in the briefing.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance | Office 365 E5/A5/G5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer Key | Included | Included |

claims.claim: For multiple workloads, the tenant needs at least as many Customer Key licences as Exchange-licensed or Teams-licensed users, whichever count is greater.
claims.quote: Because data encryption policies apply at the tenant level, your tenant must have at least as many Customer Key licenses as users assigned Exchange or Teams licenses—whichever is greater.

claims.claim: The tenant bears the Azure costs associated with the prerequisite subscriptions and key vaults.
claims.quote: The cost of operations is the same for both; so, the only price difference comes from the monthly cost of each HSM-protected key. For pricing details, see Key Vault pricing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The exporting eDiscovery user requires Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5.
claims.quote: To export content in eDiscovery, assign the eDiscovery user a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: SharePoint exports additionally require the account to have Microsoft SharePoint E3, or items might not export as expected.
claims.quote: When exporting SharePoint content, the account must also have a Microsoft SharePoint E3 license; otherwise, SharePoint items might not export as expected.

claims.claim: Administrators and investigators using eDiscovery direct export are affected.
claims.quote: Admins and investigators using Microsoft Purview eDiscovery Direct Export

claims.claim: The notice introduces no new toggle and says existing DEPs govern the behaviour.
claims.quote: Behavior is governed by existing Data Encryption Policies; no new toggle is introduced, but encryption is controlled through CMK configuration.

claims.claim: No self-service admin UI or API is documented for tenant enablement of CMK direct export.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery CMK PowerShell enable' and 'eDiscovery CMK Graph enable customer managed key'; opened edisc-search-export and read MC1289726. Enablement requires Microsoft-side configuration by support; no self-service UI or API was documented.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for assigning the tenant's multi-workload DEP.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Customer Key multi-workload admin center assign policy'; opened customer-key-manage and customer-key-set-up. Assignment is documented through Exchange Online PowerShell; search results showed no admin UI for that assignment.

claims.claim: Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID> assigns the tenant's multi-workload DEP rather than checking its status.
claims.quote:
Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID>
Replace <PolicyName or ID> with the name or GUID of the policy.

claims.claim: The Customer Key prerequisites specify Exchange admin permissions for DEP operations through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Permissions: Exchange admin permissions (all DEP operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell)

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The eDiscovery export page does not specify which DEP type satisfies its PolicyAssigned prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery direct export DEP type'; opened edisc-search-export, customer-key-set-up and customer-key-manage. The export page requires MDEP and PolicyAssigned but does not name a DEP type or an assignment cmdlet.

claims.claim: The Customer Key pages say all Customer Key operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Permissions: Exchange admin permissions (all Customer Key operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell)
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'Multi-workload DEP assignment uses Exchange Online PowerShell and requires Exchange admin permissions.' The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/customer-key-manage also directs SharePoint configuration through SharePoint PowerShell and Key Vault operations through Azure PowerShell.

claims.claim: Rolling back Customer Key for multiple workloads requires a Microsoft Support request.
claims.quote: If you no longer want to use Customer Key with multi-workload data encryption policies (DEPs), submit a support request through Microsoft Support.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how to see whether a particular direct export package received CMK encryption in the report or portal.
claims.quote: Searched: 'eDiscovery CMK report encryption status'; opened edisc-search-export, edisc-process-report and edisc-process-report-use; searched the latter for CMK, customer-managed and encryption. Found no package-level CMK indicator.

controlChecks.governs: The data encryption policy assigned to the tenant, a prerequisite for CMK direct export
